A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 39 pages of each version, including Appendix A, are readable and directly matchable across text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A.5 report original selective and clinical unlearning experiments, ablations, model-composition results and timing measurements.

after.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A.5 retain these original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons, clinical evaluations, ablations and model-composition measurements.

M1.justification: The bilevel objective, perturbed sign-gradient boundary search, relabeling, outer optimization, optional loss components and model-composition procedures are unchanged (Sections 2.1–2.4 and 3.4; Algorithms 1–3).

E1.justification: Both retain the same CIFAR-10, FashionMNIST, MRI, fundus and periocular evaluations, plus the ultrasound heatmaps in Appendix Figure 11. Class-based, imaging-device and anatomical forgetting scenarios also match.

E2.justification: Retrain, Finetune, NegGrad, CFK, EUK, SCRUB and Boundary participate in the same corresponding comparisons, including Table 1 and Appendix Tables 6–11.

E3.justification: The 80/20 splits, architectures, training budgets, augmentations, forget-set fractions, evaluation metrics and MIA attack procedure remain unchanged (Sections 2.6–2.7 and 3; Appendix A.5).

E4.justification: Both contain the same logit/remain-loss ablations, clinical case studies, decision-boundary visualizations, model-composition analyses and hyperparameter sweeps (Sections 3.2–3.4; Appendix A.5).

E5.justification: Five-fold MIA cross-validation and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting are unchanged (Section 2.7; Table 1; Appendix Tables 6–11). No seed, repetition-count or additional statistical-test information is introduced.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and plotted findings match throughout. For example, Table 1 retains the proposed method's R-Acc/F-Acc of 0.51/0.10 for CFP-Clinic and 0.91/0.38 for Oculoplastics. Appendix scores, composition results and timings also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, bilevel formulation, Lemmas 2.1 and 2.3, Corollary 2.2, Theorem 2.4 and proofs in Appendices A.1–A.4 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain identical claims about convergence guarantees, tunable forgetting–retention tradeoffs, compositional reuse and clinical model maintenance beyond privacy applications.

C2.justification: Interpretations of subgroup forgetting, retraining, retention tradeoffs and poor CFP-Clinic separability are unchanged. The discussion of applicability to vision transformers and broader clinical settings is also retained (Section 4; Appendix A.5.2).

D1.justification: Training hyperparameters, GPU hardware, pseudocode, dataset-curation details, tuning grids and timing disclosures match (Section 2.6; Algorithms 1–3; Appendix A.5). No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: All 47 references are retained, with unchanged positioning relative to Boundary Unlearning and prior privacy-oriented research. No cited work or substantive novelty relationship is added or removed.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1, 28 May 2025, to v2, 11 Nov 2025. The title, displayed authors, prose, terminology, section ordering and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–12 and Tables 1–11 retain their designs, captions, labels and placement. All embedded figure images are identical, and visual inspection shows unchanged document layout.

improvement.justification: v2 retains the same methods, proofs, experimental evidence, reproducibility details and limitations, including the appendices. The updated version/date stamp does not materially improve or diminish scientific quality, clarity or presentation.
